title: Pear Upside-Down Cake
changes_from_base: Fanned pear slices on a ginger brown-sugar caramel, cinnamon in the batter; about 5 minutes longer.
summary: This follows the classic upside-down method, with fanned pear slices set over a ginger-spiked brown-sugar caramel and cinnamon folded through the batter, baking for about 5 minutes longer than the original.
equipment: 23 cm round cake tin (5 cm deep, not loose-based), base-lined and greased
stand mixer or electric hand whisk
serving plate larger than the tin

ingredients.item: firm-ripe pears, peeled, cored and sliced 6 mm
fine sea salt or table salt
cake flour (or plain flour; see note)
ingredients.note: plain flour works with a slightly firmer crumb

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) with a shelf in the middle, and let it heat for at least 20 minutes before baking. Starting with a fully heated oven helps the sponge rise steadily around the fruit rather than cooking unevenly.

steps.title: Make the ginger caramel
steps.text: Simmer the butter, brown sugar and ginger together for 2 minutes until thick, then pour into the tin. Fan the pear slices over the caramel in overlapping circles, working from the edge inward. The warming spice infuses straight into the caramel as it bakes, flavouring the fruit from underneath.

steps.title: Cream the butter and sugar
steps.text: Whisk the butter, caster sugar and salt together for 3-4 minutes until light, pale and fluffy, laying the groundwork for the ginger-spiced sponge above the pears. Add the eggs one at a time, then beat in the vanilla and cinnamon. This step whips air into the fat, which the baking powder later expands in the oven.

steps.title: Fold in flour and milk
steps.text: On low speed, mix in the flour and baking powder in two additions, alternating with the milk, stopping as soon as the batter turns smooth. Overmixing at this point can toughen the crumb, so a gentle hand pays off.

steps.title: Spoon batter over the pears
steps.text: Spoon the batter over the fanned pears and spread it gently out to the edges, taking care not to disturb the pattern underneath. A careful touch here keeps the fruit arrangement intact for the finished cake.

steps.title: Bake until golden
steps.text: Bake for 45-50 minutes, a little longer than the classic version, until golden, springy and a skewer comes out clean from the centre. Pears release more moisture than the usual pineapple topping, so the extra time lets the sponge fully set.

steps.title: Cool for exactly 10 minutes
steps.text: Leave the cake in the tin for exactly 10 minutes. The ginger caramel is still runny at this stage, letting the pears release cleanly; cooling any longer lets it set and grip the fruit in place.

steps.title: Turn out and serve
steps.text: Run a knife around the edge, set a serving plate larger than the tin on top, and turn the cake over in one confident movement. Lift away the tin, press back any pear slices that have stuck, and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Slice the pears to an even 6mm thickness so they cook through at the same rate as the sponge above them.
Cook the ginger caramel until it's visibly thickened before adding the pears, otherwise a thin topping can seep out when the cake is turned over.
Choose firm-ripe pears rather than very soft ones – they hold their shape better once baked and flipped.
Don't leave the cake in the tin longer than the 10 minutes stated, or the caramel sets and grips the fruit in place.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for up to 1 day, or in the fridge for up to 3 days. Wrapped slices freeze for up to 2 months; thaw at room temperature and warm gently until just heated through before serving.
